transcript.text: Hi everyone. I wanted to bring up an important issue with the independent-study draft plan before it goes to the principal. The Earth Science course includes four required hands-on labs that cannot be replaced by online modules. Each lab must be supervised in person for exactly 90 minutes. I confirmed this against the department's lab safety checklist this week, but the checklist hasn't been attached to the independent-study request yet. We need to figure out how to incorporate these supervised labs into the plan before the principal reviews it.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I should mention that during my intake call with the student's family this week, they confirmed the student cannot attend Tuesday afternoon meetings due to a recurring work obligation. Saturday at 10:00 a.m. is the reliable meeting time for them. I haven't updated the draft schedule yet to reflect this.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thank you both for raising these important issues before this reaches my desk. Ms. Ibarra, the four supervised hands-on labs at 90 minutes each are a critical gap in the draft — I appreciate you catching that against the lab safety checklist. Mr. Chen, the Tuesday afternoon scheduling conflict is also significant; if Saturday at 10:00 a.m. is the family's reliable time, the draft needs to be updated accordingly. Before I can approve any independent-study plan, I'm required to have the supervising teacher and counselor review the draft. So here's what I'd like to see happen: first, update the draft to include the four in-person supervised lab sessions and change the check-in meetings to Saturday at 10:00 a.m. Then, route the revised draft to the supervising teacher and counselor for their review. Once I have their feedback and the updated plan in front of me, I can make an approval decision. Does that work for everyone?
